title: August 2026 Housing Market Brief
headline: Inflation outpaced home-value growth as permitting increased
summary: July data show Los Angeles metro home values rising more slowly than local consumer prices. Preliminary permit authorizations increased in both Los Angeles and Orange Counties, while metropolitan for-sale inventory and asking-rent growth remained below the Lab's materiality thresholds.
reconstruction_note: Prepared retrospectively from the Lab's current validated extracts using only observations dated through July 2026. This is not a contemporaneous August release snapshot, and values may incorporate provider revisions accepted after August 31.

source_releases.provider: U.S. Census Bureau Building Permits Survey

sections.question: Are home values keeping pace with local inflation?
sections.answer: No. Los Angeles metro home values increased 0.9% from one year earlier, while LA-area CPI-U increased 3.4%. The implied inflation-adjusted change was -2.4%.
evidence: Zillow's typical Los Angeles metro home value was $964,934, compared with $956,028 one year earlier.
LA-area CPI-U was 355.311, up 3.4% from one year earlier.
sections.sources: Zillow Research + U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
sections.caveat: The real change is a purchasing-power comparison, not an affordability measure. LA-area CPI-U covers Los Angeles and Orange Counties and is not seasonally adjusted.

sections.question: Is residential permitting increasing?
sections.answer: Yes in the year-to-date preliminary series. Authorizations increased 49.7% in Los Angeles County and 19.3% in Orange County from the same months of 2025.
evidence: Los Angeles County jurisdictions authorized 17,045 units, compared with 11,384 in January through July 2025.
Orange County jurisdictions authorized 4,047 units, compared with 3,391 in January through July 2025.
sections.sources: U.S. Census Bureau Building Permits Survey
sections.caveat: Current-year observations are preliminary and may be revised or imputed. Permits are authorizations, not housing starts or completions.

sections.question: Has metropolitan inventory shifted materially?
sections.answer: Not under the Lab's 5% reporting threshold. Los Angeles metro for-sale inventory decreased 1.6% from one year earlier.
evidence: Zillow reported 25,970 for-sale listings, compared with 26,379 one year earlier.
sections.caveat: This is a descriptive metropolitan estimate and does not identify the cause of the change.

sections.question: Are asking rents accelerating?
sections.answer: No material acceleration was detected. Los Angeles metro typical asking rent increased 1.5% from one year earlier, just below the Lab's exact 1.5% reporting threshold before rounding.
evidence: Zillow's typical asking rent was $2,944, compared with $2,901 one year earlier; the unrounded increase was 1.482%.
sections.caveat: This is a descriptive metropolitan estimate and does not identify the cause of the change.
